Petra Fortress, Tsikhisdziri

Byzantine fortress ruins on a rocky headland above the sea, between Kobuleti and Batumi.

Time needed
1 h
From Tbilisi
355 km · 5:20
Road
Paved
Car needed
Economy class
Season
All year
Entry
free

Petra fortress stands at Tsikhisdziri on a rocky headland that drops straight to the sea. It is one of those rare places where a historic monument and a coastal view occupy the same point.

The fortress was built in the sixth century under the emperor Justinian as a Byzantine strongpoint on the eastern Black Sea coast. The name Petra means "rock" in Greek and describes the site exactly. It is best known from the Lazic Wars: in the middle of the sixth century the confrontation between Byzantium and Sasanian Persia reached its climax here, and Petra changed hands several times during the campaigns.

Today you will find on the site:

  • Remains of walls and towers, partly consolidated
  • The foundations of a basilica on the upper part of the headland
  • A view over the Black Sea and the coastline in both directions

The visit is short — an hour is entirely enough — and it fits neatly into a drive between Kobuleti and Batumi. The site is open, the infrastructure minimal, but in exchange it is almost never crowded, which is unusual for anything on this stretch of coast in summer.

Practical advice

Late afternoon is the best time, when the sun drops toward the sea — that is the point of the view here. The paths are stony and steep in places, so wear closed shoes; after rain the rock becomes genuinely slippery. There is very little shade and midday in summer is hot. Park in the marked area beside the main road. Cafes and shops are along the road toward Kobuleti, and the nearest ATM is in Kobuleti itself, about ten minutes away.

How to get there from Tbilisi

It is about 355 km and five hours twenty from Tbilisi. The whole route follows the E60: Gori, Khashuri, the Rikoti section, Kutaisi, Samtredia and then down the coast toward Kobuleti. Tsikhisdziri sits directly on the Kobuleti–Batumi road, so no detour or turning back is needed. The access is paved and an economy car is entirely sufficient. Fill up in Kobuleti or Batumi; both are ten to fifteen kilometres away, and there is a station on the main road nearby.
